claims.statement: Bazedoxifene is not marketed as a standalone drug in the United States; it is FDA-approved only as the fixed-dose combination product DUAVEE (bazedoxifene 20 mg / conjugated estrogens 0.45 mg), indicated in women with a uterus for treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms of menopause and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis. The label carries a boxed warning and directs use for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals.

claims.statement: Bazedoxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) with tissue-selective activity: it acts as a competitive estrogen-receptor antagonist in breast and endometrial tissue (antiproliferative effect), while acting as an estrogen-receptor agonist in bone, favorably affecting bone turnover and lipid metabolism.

claims.statement: In a 3-year randomized, placebo- and active(raloxifene)-controlled phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, bazedoxifene significantly reduced the risk of new vertebral fractures compared with placebo; the same body of trial evidence reported no evidence of endometrial or breast stimulation with bazedoxifene. Adverse effects including hot flushes (vasodilatation), leg cramps, and venous thromboembolic events were significantly more frequent with bazedoxifene (and with raloxifene) than with placebo.

claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled phase 3 study, venous thromboembolism (VTE) rates were higher with bazedoxifene than placebo: any-VTE incidence was 2.8 per 1,000 women-years with bazedoxifene 20 mg and 2.9 per 1,000 women-years with bazedoxifene 40 mg, versus 1.7 per 1,000 women-years with placebo; deep vein thrombosis specifically occurred at 1.7 (20 mg) and 2.0 (40 mg) per 1,000 women-years with bazedoxifene versus 0.2 with placebo. VTE risk did not differ significantly between bazedoxifene and raloxifene, and absolute risk was described as low, with an attributable risk of about 1 additional VTE case per 1,000 women-years.

claims.statement: Bazedoxifene is listed by anti-doping literature among SERMs (alongside clomiphene, raloxifene, tamoxifen, and toremifene) prohibited by WADA and used in unsupervised, non-approved post-cycle therapy (PCT) after anabolic-androgenic steroid cessation to counter estrogen-driven effects such as gynecomastia; a 2025 qualitative analysis of illicit PCT products flags bazedoxifene as a newer-generation SERM 'expected to soon become more popular in the illegal market,' but did not detect it in the illicit samples it actually analyzed. No controlled human evidence establishes safety or efficacy of bazedoxifene for anabolic-steroid PCT, gynecomastia prevention, or any bodybuilding/performance use; bazedoxifene's only human efficacy and safety data come from postmenopausal-osteoporosis and menopausal-vasomotor-symptom trials in older women, a population and physiology very different from steroid-using men.

context.population: anabolic-androgenic steroid users seeking unsupervised post-cycle therapy
context.route: oral (as used in approved product; illicit-market formulation/route not verified)
context.formulation: illicit/gray-market bazedoxifene-containing products (not FDA-approved for this use)
context.useCase: unapproved post-cycle therapy / anti-estrogen use for gynecomastia prevention in steroid users
